---
title: "Question 9: Combine Three Inputs"
format: dashboard
server: shiny
---

```{r}
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)

# Built-in U.S. economic data, so no separate CSV file is needed
data(economics, package = "ggplot2")
econ <- economics
econ_long <- econ |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(pce, psavert, uempmed, unemploy),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    pce = "Personal consumption spending (millions of dollars)",
    psavert = "Personal savings rate (percent)",
    uempmed = "Median unemployment duration (weeks)",
    unemploy = "People unemployed (thousands)"))
```

## {.sidebar}

### Dashboard controls

```{r}
selectInput("measure", "Economic measure", choices = unique(econ_long$measure), selected = unique(econ_long$measure)[1])
sliderInput("years", "Year range", min = 1967, max = 2015, value = c(1990, 2015), sep = "")
radioButtons("chart", "Second chart", choices = c("Distribution" = "hist", "Yearly average" = "year"), inline = TRUE)
```

Try changing the measure, years, and second chart.

## Trends

### Row {height=65%}

```{r}
plotlyOutput("trend")
```

### Row {height=35%}

```{r}
DTOutput("data_table")
```

## Data view

### Row {height=100%}

```{r}
plotlyOutput("second_plot")
```

```{r}
#| context: server
filtered <- reactive(filter(econ_long, measure == input$measure, year(date) >= input$years[1], year(date) <= input$years[2]))
output$trend <- renderPlotly({
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(date, value)) + geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = input$measure) + theme_minimal()
  ggplotly(p)
})
output$second_plot <- renderPlotly({
  if (input$chart == "hist") {
    p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(value)) + geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "orange") + labs(x = input$measure, y = "Number of months")
  } else {
    annual <- filtered() |> mutate(year = year(date)) |> group_by(year) |> summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
    p <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, value)) + geom_line(color = "darkgreen") + geom_point() + labs(x = "Year", y = "Annual average")
  }
  ggplotly(p + theme_minimal())
})
output$data_table <- renderDT({ datatable(filtered(), options = list(pageLength = 8)) })
```
